title: Uncomplicated malaria (adult) — Nigeria
presentation: Fever or history of fever, chills, headache, myalgia.
Residence in / travel to a malaria-endemic area.
redFlags: Respiratory distress, jaundice, dark urine, severe anaemia, shock.
Inability to tolerate orals or repeated vomiting.

diagnostics.rationale: Confirm parasitologically before treatment — do not treat on clinical suspicion alone.

management.detail: Treat only after a positive RDT or microscopy.

AL is the first-line ACT for uncomplicated falciparum malaria per the Nigeria Standard Treatment Guidelines, Federal Ministry of Health. Dosing is weight-banded — use the national weight-based dosing chart; do not estimate. Take with fatty food.
Return immediately if fever persists or any red flag appears.

references.label: Nigeria Standard Treatment Guidelines, Federal Ministry of Health

title: Severe malaria — Nigeria
presentation: Confirmed/suspected malaria PLUS any danger sign (coma, convulsions, respiratory distress, shock, severe anaemia, jaundice, hypoglycaemia, inability to tolerate orals).
redFlags: Any feature of severe malaria is itself an emergency — treat and refer.

management.detail: IV/IM artesunate is the treatment of choice for severe malaria. Dose is weight-based — use the national chart; do not estimate.
Give pre-referral rectal artesunate where injectable treatment/transport is delayed.
After ≥24h parenteral therapy and able to tolerate orals, complete a full oral ACT course.
Treat hypoglycaemia, seizures, severe anaemia; refer urgently.

references.label: Nigeria Standard Treatment Guidelines, Federal Ministry of Health

title: Childhood pneumonia (under-5) — Nigeria
presentation: Cough or difficult breathing with fast breathing for age (IMCI).
redFlags: General danger signs: unable to drink/breastfeed, vomiting everything, convulsions, lethargic/unconscious.
Chest indrawing, stridor in a calm child, central cyanosis — severe pneumonia, refer.

diagnostics.test: Respiratory rate + danger-sign assessment (IMCI); pulse oximetry if available
diagnostics.rationale: Classify non-severe vs severe to decide oral vs referral.

management.detail: Per IMCI/national guidance, treat fast-breathing pneumonia with oral amoxicillin. Dose is weight/age-banded — use the national dosing chart; do not estimate.
Give a first dose of an appropriate antibiotic and oxygen if available, then refer urgently.
Continue feeding/fluids; review in 3 days or sooner if worse.

references.label: Nigeria Standard Treatment Guidelines, Federal Ministry of Health
WHO Pocket book of hospital care for children, 2nd ed

title: Acute diarrhoea + dehydration (under-5) — Nigeria
redFlags: Severe dehydration (lethargy, sunken eyes, very slow skin pinch), blood in stool, persistent diarrhoea, severe malnutrition — refer/escalate.

diagnostics.rationale: Classify no/some/severe dehydration to select Plan A/B/C.

management.detail: Low-osmolarity ORS per IMCI plan (A/B/C) plus zinc for 10–14 days. Use the national age/weight-based amounts; do not estimate.
Continue breastfeeding/feeding throughout.
Antibiotics only for dysentery (bloody stool) or cholera per national guidance — not for routine watery diarrhoea.
Plan C IV rehydration and refer if not improving.

references.label: Nigeria Standard Treatment Guidelines, Federal Ministry of Health

title: Pulmonary tuberculosis — Nigeria
presentation: Cough ≥2 weeks, fever, night sweats, weight loss; or any duration in a person living with HIV / close contact.
redFlags: Haemoptysis, respiratory distress, suspected TB meningitis or miliary TB — escalate.

diagnostics.rationale: WHO-recommended initial test, incl. rifampicin resistance.
Test all people with TB for HIV.

management.detail: Drug-susceptible pulmonary TB: 2 months HRZE then 4 months HR, per the national TB programme. Use weight-band fixed-dose combinations from the national chart; do not estimate.
Start ART in all TB/HIV patients; give cotrimoxazole preventive therapy.
Support adherence; refer rifampicin-resistant/MDR-TB to the programme pathway.

references.label: Nigeria Standard Treatment Guidelines, Federal Ministry of Health

title: HIV — first-line ART — Nigeria
presentation: Confirmed HIV (national testing algorithm). Assess for TB, cryptococcal disease and other OIs at diagnosis.
redFlags: Advanced HIV disease with new headache/fever/neurology — assess for cryptococcal/TB meningitis and refer.

diagnostics.test: Confirmatory HIV testing + baseline CD4 + viral load
diagnostics.rationale: Confirm diagnosis; assess advanced disease; establish monitoring baseline.

management.detail: Offer ART to all people living with HIV regardless of CD4; rapid initiation once ready.
Dolutegravir-based TLD is the preferred first-line regimen. Use the national fixed-dose formulation; paediatric regimens per national weight bands — do not estimate.
Cotrimoxazole and TPT where indicated; viral load at 6 and 12 months then annually (target <1000 copies/mL).
PrEP for substantial risk; PEP within 72h; lifelong ART in pregnancy/breastfeeding (PMTCT).

references.label: Nigeria Standard Treatment Guidelines, Federal Ministry of Health
